news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

A single factory in France that makes specialized rayon, the material used in Hawaiian shirts, is holding up production of vital Patriot missiles, infuriating US suppliers, according to a report.

The supplier, ArianeGroup, based in the heart of Bordeaux wine country, produces carbonized rayon fabric for use in space rockets and ballistic missiles, which is then shipped to Kansas-based Park Aerospace for further processing.

But recently, ArianeGroup has warned that supplies are limited, leaving the US munitions industry tearing its hair out, with Pentagon pressure reportedly having zero effect on ending the logjam.

“They’re a French company. They can’t be bullied. They’ll just shut down on you,” Brian Shore, a spokesperson for Park Aerospace, told the Wall Street Journal.

The form of carbonized rayon, available only from Park Aerospace, is capable of withstanding temperatures in the thousands of degrees and is crucial for use in advanced Patriot interceptors, one of the most sought-after missile defense systems in the world.

Each $4 million interceptor takes roughly two years and hundreds of components to make, with the rayon used in the latest system made first as a thread at a factory in the Czech Republic owned by a Thailand-based chemicals conglomerate, before being sent to France for carbonization.

But with the supply chain now dependent on multiple foreign contractors with often no ready American alternatives, chokepoints are common.

One defense executive said the process of preparing for a weapons surge now requires five years of planning.

Another compared the industry to pushing a basketball through a garden hose.

“There’s a lot of testing that’s involved. You could go down the path for two years, everything’s looking good, then at the last test it fails, and now you’re back to the drawing board,” Shore said.

Park Aerospace pledged a $5 million advance to fund a new production line at the ArianeGroup factory, which is expected to be ready by 2028.

ArianeGroup has also signed a preliminary agreement to build a factory in the US, backed by a promised additional $25 million advance from Park Aerospace, expected to be finished in around 2030.

“The big problem is that nobody wants to wait three-and-a-half years,” Shore said.

Many blame the delays on Clinton-era slashes to military spending made after the end of the Cold War, which saw the consolidation of the American aerospace and defense industries.

Between 1993 and 2015, the number of top-tier American defense companies fell from 51 to just five primary contractors.

Specialized manufacturers and machine shops in the US often went out of business or moved away from defense work, part of the broader shrinking of the US industrial sector under Clinton.

The number of small businesses in the US defense industrial base shrank by 40% between 2012 and 2022, when the Pentagon published a report on the subject.

More than 70% of second-tier suppliers for the PAC-3, the newest generation of Patriot missiles, also supply THAAD, another missile interceptor that targets ballistic missiles.

This means that failure at one supplier — such as a workers’ strike, a natural disaster, or bankruptcy — could have knock-on effects on the entire process.

In a bid to make this right, the Pentagon signed seven-year deals with Lockheed Martin and L3Harris to accelerate production of the most advanced Patriot missiles and their rocket motors to accelerate production amid the ongoing Iran conflict and restore the US’s missile stockpile depleted by the Ukraine-Russia war.

It is also reaching out directly to third- and fourth-tier suppliers to try to ease bottlenecks further down the chain.

“[The Pentagon is] continually working on supply chain resilience and qualifying new suppliers,” it said in a statement.

L3Harris — which has also been blamed for last week’s FAA systems glitch that ground flights on Friday — said it is confident it will “maintain the materials needed to produce at quantities required, through at least the end of our 7-year framework agreement,” in a statement.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

The best thing Fernando Mendoza has going for him Sunday in Denver might be the same thing the Broncos have going for them. Both sides got a good look at what happened to the Raiders rookie against Seattle.

Presumably, both sides hit the rewind button.

For Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph, the attraction is obvious. The Seahawks sacked Mendoza six times in his first NFL start. Any coach with a rested pass rush and a home crowd willing to make life miserable for a visiting quarterback would be interested in how they went about it.

For Mendoza, the part worth rewinding might come a second or two before he hit the ground. What did he see when he came to the line? What changed when he got the ball? And where could he have gone with it once it did?

The Broncos present some big-time challenges in that regard.

“It’s one of the top defenses in the league for a reason,” Mendoza said. “So they are very good, they’re very sound and I respect them a lot.”

Coach Klint Kubiak is confident the rookie will process and adapt accordingly.

“His approach has been excellent since he got here,” Kubiak said. “He’s a competitor. It’s his first NFL start. I thought he played well enough for us to win, especially in that first half, and we didn’t close it out in the second half.”

A week ago, those were questions he had to answer against Mike Macdonald’s defense without the benefit of a single NFL start. On Sunday, there’s at least a chance Joseph asks him something he’s heard before.

Consider what Denver can take from the way Seattle made Mendoza account for pressure. A linebacker walking up to the line gives the quarterback something to think about. Put one in each gap alongside the center and now the quarterback and his protection have some decisions to make.

The beauty of it for Denver is that neither linebacker has to come. If Mendoza hurries a throw over the middle to beat a blitz and finds a linebacker dropping into the very window he picked out, Joseph will have gotten what he wanted without sending anybody extra.

So where’s the opportunity for Mendoza? Start with what happens if that linebacker comes.

Somebody just vacated a valuable piece of real estate. A receiver breaking inside behind him can give Mendoza a throw he can make with his feet set, before the rush has much say in the matter. Six or 7 yards on first down would do wonders for an offense that spent too much of Sunday trying to figure out third-and-long.

There’s a bigger throw available, too, if Denver decides to crowd the line and leave a cornerback outside with no safety behind him. That’s a chance to give Tre Tucker a ball down the sideline. The trick is confirming the safety really did come down. Seattle gave Mendoza firsthand experience with how much a picture can change between the time a quarterback calls for the ball and the time it reaches his hands.

Getting Tucker involved would go a long way, especially if Brock Bowers’ ankle injury keeps him on the sideline. Tucker’s ability to stretch the field, and Mendoza’s willingness to take some chances on those long throws, could help open things up for the run game and the short and intermediate passing game.

“There are a lot of variables and what our coach always emphasizes making sure we’re taking the positive gain,” Mendoza said. “However, those deep shots and those explosives are what can help us win the game. And so, I mean, it’s really play-by-play, and I look forward to taking a look at the shots we have this weekend.”

Lost in those six sacks is a reason to believe Mendoza can make some of those throws. He completed 11 of 13 passes in the first half against Seattle and got the ball to eight receivers. He already knows what it feels like to take what an NFL defense gives him and move on to the next play.

Kubiak can help him get back to that. Give Mendoza an early throw on a moving pocket. Change where Denver’s edge rushers expect to find him. And if the Broncos are getting upfield in a hurry, a well-timed screen gives those rushers an invitation to keep right on going.

Some of which requires a seamless process well ahead of the snap.

“I was very pleased with him getting out of the huddle, him making the correct checks, the correct calls,” Kubiak said. “That’s what he has shown in practice, his ability to do that and to be able to run the show that way. There’s room for growth, but in his first start, I thought that he operated the game like he does in practice.”

Of course, there’s a limit to what anybody can draw up if the Raiders run for 65 yards on 24 carries again. Joseph had a bye week to study the Raiders. He hardly needed all of it to see the advantage in making Mendoza throw on downs when everyone in the stadium knows he has to.

Denver figures to make the rookie prove he can solve some of the problems Seattle put on tape. Fair enough.

But if the Broncos want to borrow from the Seahawks, Mendoza gets something out of the deal, too. Somewhere in all that film of what went wrong is a throw he’d love to have back.

Sunday, he just might get it.

“The most important thing is how he’s playing the game. We’ll coach up everything,” Kubiak said. “But like I said, and like I told Fernando, I was pleased because of the preparation that he put in. The things that he did in practice showed up in the game, and he’s going to have a lot of things to learn and grow from.”

"بنابراین آنها بسیار خوب هستند، آنها بسیار سالم هستند و من برای آنها احترام زیادی قائل هستم."
مربی کلینت کوبیاک مطمئن است که بازیکن تازه کار بر این اساس پردازش می کند و سازگار خواهد شد. کوبیاک گفت: "رویکرد او از زمانی که به اینجا رسیده عالی بوده است." او یک رقیب است. این اولین شروع او در NFL است. من فکر می‌کردم که او به اندازه کافی خوب بازی کرد تا ما پیروز شویم، به خصوص در نیمه اول، و در نیمه دوم آن را نبستیم.»

San Francisco has approved its first gay bathhouse in nearly four decades after the AIDS epidemic led to closures of nearly two dozen locations in the 1980s.

The San Francisco Planning Commission recently voted to allow the conversion of a 7,516-square-foot non-residential, two-story building, at 40 12th St. into an “Adult Sex Venue” called Sanctum Baths.

Located near the city’s Leather and LGBTQ Cultural District, it will be the first gay bathhouse in 40 years and the first authorized since the city changed its law in 2022, the San Francisco Chronicle reported.

The project’s developer, Kevin Born, said when he saw all the foot traffic at a similar bathhouse in nearby Berkeley, it just made good business sense to open in San Francisco.

“It was staggering. If I would bet on anything, the male libido is something I would bet on,” Born, who is straight, told the San Francisco Standard.

“First and foremost, I think it’s a good business model.”

Plans for the bathhouse include 10 private rooms, a 24-person steam room and a 25-person Jacuzzi, along with showers, private changing facilities and lounge areas.

Planning documents show that the project has requested obscuring some of the building’s windows while others will remain fully transparent.

“We believe the project can honor SF’s LGBT history while demonstrating a contemporary modern building around health, professional and neighborhood accountability,” Born said.

“This is part of their culture and their lifestyle and how they find intimacy. I like the peace of providing a place where people can come and have their community.”

San Francisco had about 20 gay bathhouses in the early ’80s. But the spread of HIV and AIDS fueled fears about transmission, the city said.

“Promoting legal, safe, and private adult sex venues is viewed by members of the LGBTQ community as a way to overcome the lingering stigma of a painful chapter in the history of the city’s queer community, by once again welcoming these safe and identity-affirming spaces into our city,”  Vincent Page, associate planner for the city, said at the San Francisco Planning Commission’s meeting on the development.

The city also pointed to the advances in drugs that both “reduce risk of HIV infection, and that prevent those living with HIV from developing AIDS” in the proposal to allow for it to operate.

Born said he hopes to open the bathhouse by late next year.

An accused rapist therapist who vanished for months with a teen boy she preyed on “like a wolf” was busted with him while drunk driving, according to a lawsuit.

Sofia Drotts, 26, a behavioral health clinician for the child at Contra Costa County Juvenile Hall in the Bay Area, was hit with a slew of felony charges in July.

But, according to the new lawsuit, she was released then rearrested, then released against multiple times over the past few months all while breaking a judge’s ruling not to meet up with the boy.

Civil rights attorney John Burris filed a federal lawsuit against the county on Tuesday and detailed horrific allegations against Drotts, who is nine years older than her alleged victim.

Burris said her latest arrest came on October 25 when she was caught by CHP officers speeding while drunk driving with the child just after midnight.

Burris also claimed she preyed on boys like a “wolf” in a hen house and made the youngster “act out erotic feelings and engage in sexual intimacy,” according to the suit.

“A female sexual predator was turned loose on very needy young teenagers. Assigning this woman to work with impressionable young men was like assigning a wolf to guard a hen house,” civil rights attorney Burris wrote in a statement.

Drotts first met the victim while he was in custody at John Davis Juvenile Hall in Martinez between 2024 and April 2026 when he was 14 or 15, according to his attorneys.

County officials assigned her to counsel the boy, but she ended up having the boy “act out erotic feelings and engage in sexual intimacy,” according to the lawsuit.

Even after the boy was released on probation, Drotts and the boy continued “an inappropriate romantic, physical, and unlawful relationship that has continued into present day,” they claimed.

Drotts also schemed to build the trust of the victim’s mother over the course of long phone calls, by assuring her that her son was making excellent progress while he was incarcerated, Burris claimed.

She continued seeing the boy and his mother as a county therapist, while also meeting him illicitly in her car and in her San Francisco apartment, where the boy had begun to spend the night, Burris claimed.

The suit says Drotts “exploited the absolute power imbalance of her position as a mandatory therapist in order to groom, harass, and abuse John Doe,” between May 2025 and November 2026.

“The duplicitous nature of it is really outrageous,” Burris said. “She’s engaged in this nefarious conduct, and she’s covering her tracks with different kinds of lies.”

Prosecutors in July charged Drotts with unlawful sexual intercourse, oral copulation of a person under 18 years of age, sexual penetration by a foreign object and possession of child pornography.

The DA’s office filed more charges after the October hearing, including DUI, willful child cruelty and disobeying a court order.

She pleaded not guilty to these at a hearing Wednesday morning.

She is being held without bail.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

The MTA is eager to wallop straphangers with another fare hike — even as Chairman Janno Lieber bragged about the cash-hungry agency saving hundreds of millions of dollars a year.

The Metropolitan Transportation Authority unveiled its final proposed $22.9 billion budget for 2027 Wednesday, touting $676 million in savings next year.

But it still projects a $58 million deficit in 2027 that balloons to nearly $1 billion by 2030 — and officials are planning to hike fares on riders in just a few months to squeeze an extra $141 million.

The MTA hasn’t announced how much subway and bus fares would go up, only that it wants the increases across subways, buses, trains and tolls to add up to 4% more revenue.

Lieber defended the hikes as “small and predictable” but admitted they won’t fix the agency’s money problems.

“Do not mistake this for like solving the MTA’s budget crisis because 2% a year is only less than half of the true inflation that we are experiencing even with the cost savings,” Lieber said after the board meeting. “So it’s small, it’s predictable but it’s not putting on the riders all the additional costs and that’s important as well.”

All the while the MTA was able to cover a $200 million subsidy that Gov. Kathy Hochul let Mayor Zohran Mamdani skip paying for city bus service this year.

Asked Tuesday whether the state would pay the MTA back the $200 million, Hochul said the agency doesn’t need it.

“There’s not a hole,” the governor insisted multiple times of the MTA’s budget when asked by reporters after an unrelated press conference, claiming the $676 million in savings was able to cover the $200 million.

But Lieber the next day at the board meeting contradicted his boss, instead claiming a pension recalculation “freed up some money” to cover the $200 million. He also admitted that “in the long run, we are going to have to pay a little bit more.”

The nonprofit Citizens Budget Commission has slammed the pension recalculation as a “gimmick” that pushes the cost of closing today’s budget gaps onto taxpayers starting in 2033.

Watchdog group Reinvent Albany pointed out that the bus subsidy money the city got to keep could easily cover what riders will be expected to fork over next year in higher fares.

“We note this raid on MTA bus is in the same neighborhood of what New York City transit riders are expected to pay in fare increases over the next 2 years,” said Rachael Fauss, a senior policy adviser at Reinvent Albany. “Raiding dedicated MTA funding meant to support transit service undermines public trust.”

Riders Wednesday railed to MTA board members that they’re the ones getting stuck with Mamdani’s unpaid bus bill.

“I don’t know where they thought they were gonna pull that money out from, but it always comes from the people,” said Jonathan Rivera, 32, a security guard who takes the subway every day.

“It stinks for people who end up commuting a lot,” Zoe Turnpaugh, 31, a grants manager, said. “They ought to give (the $200 million) back, because now it’s falling on people that commute.”

The impending fare hikes, which the November financial plan factored in for March 2027 but Lieber hinted could come in Q2 of next year, come at a time when 1 in 5 riders say they can’t afford the current $3 fare, according to a recent Community Service Society survey.

“That is crazy, because we can barely pay now,” said Lesley Duran, 27, a student who takes the subway three times a week.

Arianna Allen, 31, who works in finance and rides the subway up to four times a day, said getting around is getting more and more expensive.

“If you have a couple places to go throughout the day, you’re spending $12, $15, $20,” she said. “That’s like three, four hours of work for a lot of people.”

The transit agency’s board will ultimately have to approve the hike and its timeline.

The budget presentation showed MTA budget woes were driven by health care, fuel and paratransit costs all climbing much faster than revenue.

The flailing agency has also blown $1.03 billion on overtime through October, cruising past its own projection by $199 million — more than enough to cover next year’s fare hike for subway and bus riders.

By 2030, MTA expenses are projected to be 51% higher than in 2019, while revenue grows just 34% — a gap that has budget hawks pushing for even steeper fare hikes.

The Citizens Budget Commission called for the MTA to raise its fare and toll hikes, which come every two years, to 6% from 4% — even as they acknowledged the increases would be too much for some New Yorkers.

“This would get closer to how fast MTA expenses are growing,” CBC President Andrew Rein said. “While transit is one of New York’s best bargains, fares can still be a challenge for low-income New Yorkers.”

MTA اعلام نکرده است که کرایه مترو و اتوبوس چقدر افزایش می‌یابد، فقط می‌خواهد قطارها و اتوبوس‌ها را به 4 درصد افزایش دهد. درآمد لیبر از افزایش‌ها به‌عنوان «کوچک و قابل پیش‌بینی» دفاع کرد، اما اذعان کرد که این افزایش‌ها مشکلات مالی آژانس را حل نمی‌کنند. لیبر پس از جلسه هیئت مدیره گفت: «این را مانند حل بحران بودجه MTA اشتباه نکنید، زیرا 2 درصد در سال تنها کمتر از نیمی از تورم واقعی است که حتی با صرفه‌جویی در هزینه‌ها تجربه می‌کنیم.» بنابراین کوچک است، قابل پیش بینی است، اما تمام هزینه های اضافی را بر دوش سوارکاران نمی گذارد و این نیز مهم است. در تمام مدتی که MTA توانست یارانه 200 میلیون دلاری را پوشش دهد که فرماندار کتی هوچول به شهردار زهران ممدانی اجازه داد تا هزینه سرویس اتوبوس شهری را در سال جاری پرداخت نکند. در روز سه شنبه در پاسخ به این سوال که آیا دولت 200 میلیون دلار را به MTA بازپرداخت خواهد کرد، هوچول گفت که آژانس به آن نیازی ندارد.

A Sacramento mother and daughter were arrested Tuesday in the killing of a Citrus Heights man whose severed head was found in a trash bag.

Mary Fitzmaurice, 45, was booked into the South Placer Jail on murder charges in the death of her father, Paul Wesley Fitzmaurice Jr., who was 73 at the time of the alleged killing in 2022, authorities said.

Her 75-year-old mother, Georgia “Gwenn” Fitzmaurice, was arrested on accessory charges. The Placer County Sheriff’s Office said Wednesday the mother-daughter duo allegedly worked together to get rid of the family patriarch’s remains.

Placer County deputies were called to the Todd Valley area of Foresthill on Sept. 28, 2022, after someone found a human head in a trash bag.

Due to the decomposed state of the severed head, investigators were unable to identify the man.

An autopsy was performed in 2022, and the skull was sent to California State University, Chico. Forensic experts then developed a preliminary age and race profile of the victim. They also produced an artist’s rendering of the man’s face.

The man’s DNA was also entered into the Combined DNA Index System, known as CODIS, the national database used to match crime scene evidence. It returned no matches.

Investigators sent the DNA to Othram Labs in January 2024 for forensic genetic genealogy testing –– a technique that builds a family tree from DNA profiles to find relatives of an unidentified person.

After Othram’s work pointed to possible distant relatives, the FBI and the sheriff’s office traced the family tree. Federal agents interviewed distant relatives and collected DNA samples for comparison, which led the investigators to identify the victim as Paul Fitzmaurice Jr.

During the investigation, detectives discovered that Fitzmaurice had never been reported missing, explaining why searches of missing persons databases turned up empty for years.

Authorities said he had been living in Citrus Heights with his wife and daughter until his death.

Placer County detectives on Tuesday served a search warrant at the family’s home in Citrus Heights, and the mother-daughter duo was arrested.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Anthropic’s IPO is set for a valuation of $1.4 trillion, making it the second-largest liquidity event in modern history — and it will almost certainly result in the largest ever windfall for fringe and far-left causes.

That’s because Anthropic’s seven cofounders have pledged to donate 80% of their personal equity in the company, a commitment potentially worth over $100 billion, to philanthropic causes.

It may sound noble, but the causes will all be of their own decidedly woke choosing, driven by their adherence to the ultra-leftist pseudo-philosophy Effective Altruism — which amounts to little more than “tech bros know best.”

If you thought Jeff Bezos’ ex-wife, Mackenzie Scott’s, $26 billion to trans and pro-Palestinian causes was a spending spree; or Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan’s supposedly neutral “Zuck bucks” which poured $350 million into the 2020 election cycle, largely advantaging Democrat causes — just wait.

Anthropic co-founders Dario Amodei and his sister Daniela are unabashedly liberal — with Dario reportedly referring to Donald Trump as a “feudal warlord.”

But in case you had any doubt, an analysis found 99.8% of Anthropic’s board, founders and employees’ political donations have gone to Democrats, according to the Bull Moose Project.

I predict Democrats will drop the rallying cry to get “money out of politics” as their coffers fill with donor money from Anthropic’s newly minted billionaires.

After all, the Trump administration were the ones to stand up to Anthropic and OpenAI’s calls for greater regulations on AI, calling them out for trying to gate keep and “pull up the drawbridge” on smaller AI companies.

None of this is good for conservative causes.

And far more pernicious than overt donations to possible presidential campaigns like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez or Abdul El-Sayed will be billions funneled across a vast network of left-wing NGOs.

This is where the sausage really gets made, and where people’s opinions are shaped — whether they realize it.

“It’s not just going to be a flood of cash towards explicit political work… the second aspect here is how it’s going to affect the think tank, nonprofit, policy world,” said Aiden Buzzetti, founder and president of the Bull Moose Project.

Buzzetti warns the sheer amount of cash might mean some think tanks stop criticizing Anthropic in hopes of getting some of its money — a dangerous situation.

Alongside the founders’ personal billions, Anthropic runs its own Public Benefit Fund which it has suggested it will use to make “large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.”

If that sounds like playing god, then look no further than the founders’ beliefs.

Publicly, ahead of the IPO, Anthropic has sought to distance themselves from Effective Altruism.

But Daniela’s husband, Holden Karnofsky (who now works at Anthropic) co-founded two of the biggest EA philanthropies: GiveWell and Coefficient Giving (previously Open Philanthropy).

Amanda Askell, who led the work on Claude’s 30,000-word “constitution” shaping the AI’s behavior, was previously married to William MacAskill, one of Effective Altruism’s two founders.

As AI publication Transformer News put it, “A coming wave of Anthropic wealth could flood EA-aligned nonprofits with cash.”

Some EA causes are just downright odd — like the effort to end invertebrate suffering by providing shrimp farms with stun guns for more humane deaths.

But much of the EA money gets distributed to a variety of smaller organizations pushing social justice, such as National Bail Fund Network, who pay bonds for charged criminals and seek to abolish cash bail; Color of Change, which has advocated defunding the police; People’s Action which embraces all things anti-capitalist and the Free Migration project, which thinks even abolishing ICE isn’t enough.

No doubt, much of the money will also find its way into “AI safety,” the codeword Anthropic and others use to encourage cumbersome regulation, which will disproportionately affect their competition.

“This IPO is going to allow by a factor 10, more political spendings on AI safety,” Buzzetti added. “On this idea that AI is an existential risk to humanity.”

If it really were, then surely they’d just stop?

It never ceases to amaze me that people who have benefited so much from capitalism and free markets seem so intent on changing them. But that seems to be the story of much of modern philanthropy.

پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. "برادران فناوری بهتر می دانند." اگر فکر می کردید که همسر سابق جف بزوس، مکنزی اسکات، 26 میلیارد دلار برای اهداف ترنس و طرفدار فلسطینی ها هزینه ولخرجی است. یا مارک زاکربرگ و پریسیلا چان ظاهراً "زاک دلار" بی طرفی که 350 میلیون دلار به چرخه انتخابات 2020 سرازیر کرد، تا حد زیادی از اهداف دموکرات ها سود برد - فقط صبر کنید. بنیانگذاران آنتروپیک، داریو آمودی و خواهرش دانیلا، بی شرمانه لیبرال هستند - طبق گزارش ها، داریو از دونالد ترامپ به عنوان یک "جنگ سالار فئودال" یاد می کند.
اما اگر شک داشتید، طبق یک تحلیل، بر اساس پروژه Bull Moose، 99.8 درصد از کمک‌های مالی هیئت‌مدیره، بنیان‌گذاران و کارمندان آنتروپیک به دموکرات‌ها رفته است. من پیش‌بینی می‌کنم دموکرات‌ها با پر شدن خزانه‌هایشان از پول‌های اهداکنندگان میلیاردرهای تازه‌ای که آنتروپیک به دست آورده‌اند، فریاد تجمع را کنار بگذارند تا «پول‌ها را از سیاست خارج کنند».

Sonny Gray is back in a familiar place.

The righty pitcher is signing with the Twins on a two-year, $55 million contract that includes an opt-out after the first season, the team announced Wednesday.

Gray pitched for the Twins in 2022-23, posting a 16-13 record with a 2.90 ERA and finishing second in AL Cy Young voting in 2023.

Gray, 37, is coming off a standout season for the Red Sox, leading the majors with 18 wins and leading the American League with a .783 winning percentage. He entered free agency when the team declined its side of a mutual $30 million option for next season and Gray his $5 million buyout.

He was the top piece of the Red Sox rotation for much of 2026 while Garrett Crochet battled shoulder and lat injuries.

Gray’s Red Sox tenure ended on a less-than-happy note when he was pulled early from Game 2 of the American League wild-card series against the Yankees after throwing just 70 pitches and allowing one run in 4 ⅔ innings. The Red Sox went on to lose the game to end their season, and Gray expressed frustration with manager Chad Tracy’s decision.

“I’m the best pitcher in the American League third time through the order,” Gray said after the Sept. 30 contest. “I think that’s a fact. I would have liked to have been trusted in that moment.”

In 14 total seasons in the majors, Gray has a 143-107 record with a 3.51 ERA and 2,074 strikeouts in 2,087 innings. He has also pitched for the Athletics, Yankees, Reds, and Cardinals.

Gray’s arrival in Minnesota comes with an interesting sidenote, as the ex-Yankees hurler said his time in the Bronx wasn’t a “good situation,” and that he “never wanted to go there in the first place.” The Twins have struggled against the Yankees in recent years, going 12-27 against the Bombers since 2021.

news.originalContent:
Trials began in September for 47 French citizens who were transferred from Syria last year.

An Iraqi criminal court has sentenced six French nationals to life in prison for joining the ISIL (ISIS) group, state media reported.

The Karkh Criminal Court delivered the sentencing on Wednesday with representatives from the French embassy in attendance, the Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported, citing Iraq’s judiciary.

“With these six sentences, the total number of those convicted in this case has reached 16, all of whom are French nationals,” the judiciary said in a statement cited by INA.

All but one of the 16 convicted were sentenced to life. The court sentenced one defendant to 15 years in prison last month.

Trials began in September for 47 French citizens who were transferred from Syria last year and charged with belonging to the armed group, which controlled large parts of both countries between 2014 and 2017.

In February, Iraq received more than 5,700 ISIL detainees from over 60 countries after the United States transferred them from Syria, following years of detention in prisons run by Kurdish-led forces.

For years, Iraqi courts handed down hundreds of execution orders and life sentences to people convicted of “terrorism” offences, including foreign fighters. However, some rights groups denounced the trials as rushed and lacking due process.

Among the foreign fighters sentenced on Wednesday was Thomas Barnouin, a 45-year-old Frenchman, who said during his trial that he travelled to Syria convinced he had a religious duty and did not know ISIL would carry out attacks in France, according to AFP.

The ISIL group swept across Syria and Iraq in 2014, committing massacres and forcing women and girls into sexual slavery.

Iraq, backed by US-led forces, proclaimed victory over the group in 2017, and Kurdish-led forces supported by Washington defeated ISIL in neighbouring Syria two years later.

Iraq is nonetheless still reckoning with the group’s legacy, with mass graves being uncovered and testimonies of its brutality still to be investigated.

news.originalContent:
Public support for raising the minimum wage grows, with 78 percent of voters saying it was an important election issue.

In Washington, DC, a group of lawmakers has ramped up calls to increase the United States federal minimum wage and eliminate the subminimum wage, otherwise known as the tipped wage.

The group of 17 lawmakers, which includes current and newly elected House members, is calling for passage of the Living Wage For All Act, which has been languishing since it was introduced in April.

The legislation’s original lead sponsors include Representative Delia Ramirez of Illinois, Representative Jesus “Chuy” Garcia, also of Illinois, and Representative Analilia Mejia of New Jersey.

The bill aims to gradually raise the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour, with different timelines depending on the size of the employer.

Brad Lander, a congressman-elect from Brooklyn, New York, who says he will join the bill as a co-sponsor when the next congressional session begins in January, told Al Jazeera: “Doing it federally is the right way to go. Tying it into broader legislation that raises the minimum wage for all workers is a great approach.”

For larger employers — those with more than 500 employees nationwide or at least $1bn in annual revenue — the increase would be completed by 2031. Smaller employers would have until 2038.

After that, the minimum wage would be maintained at two-thirds of the US median hourly wage, with annual adjustments to preserve that ratio.

The bill would also eliminate the separate subminimum wage for tipped workers, currently $2.13 an hour. Under the existing framework, employers can count workers’ tips towards their minimum-wage requirements.

While several states have raised their own minimum wages, the federal rate remains $7.25 an hour, where it has stood since 2009. Washington, DC, has the highest minimum wage of any US jurisdiction, at $18.40 an hour, followed by Washington state at $17.13. However, 20 states do not have a minimum wage higher than the federal rate. Those states include Texas, Georgia and Iowa.

Laws governing the subminimum wage also vary across states. Seven states require employers to pay tipped workers the full minimum wage before tips, including Alaska, California and Nevada.

Others, including New York, have higher tipped cash wages than the federal rate but allow employers to take a tip credit, meaning they can pay workers less than the standard minimum wage as long as their tips make up the difference.

In New York, minimum wages vary by region. The rate is $17 an hour in New York City and its surrounding suburbs, and $16 an hour in the rest of the state.

For tipped workers outside the food service industry, the minimum cash wage is $14.15 in the New York City metropolitan area and $13.30 elsewhere in the state. For restaurant workers, those rates are $11.35 and $10.70, respectively.

The distinction is a point of contention for Lander.

“All workers deserve a raise. The 45 million working people who make less than $20 an hour deserve a raise, and the tipped subminimum wage is inexcusable at this point,” he said.

The subminimum wage has long been viewed as a legacy of racial and economic inequalities that disproportionately affected Black Americans. When Congress passed the Fair Labor Standards Act in 1938, establishing the first federal minimum wage, it excluded categories of workers in domestic and agricultural occupations, which disproportionately employed Black Americans.

Congress extended federal minimum-wage protections to restaurant and other service workers in 1966. But rather than requiring employers to pay tipped workers the full minimum wage, lawmakers established a separate tipped minimum wage, initially set at 50 percent of the standard federal rate. Employers could count customers’ tips towards the rest of a worker’s minimum-wage obligation. In 1996, Congress froze the federal tipped cash wage at $2.13 an hour, where it remains today.

The purchasing power of the standard federal minimum wage has also changed drastically. Adjusted for inflation, the $7.25 minimum wage in 2009 would be worth $11.32 today, meaning it has lost 36 percent of its purchasing power.

The federal minimum wage’s purchasing power peaked in 1968, when the rate was $1.60 an hour. Adjusted for inflation, that peak would be worth significantly more than the current minimum wage, representing a loss of roughly 53 percent in purchasing power.

The push to raise wages also has public support. A new poll released on Wednesday by One Fair Wage, an organisation that has long campaigned to eliminate the subminimum wage, found that 78 percent of voters considered raising the minimum wage to $25 an hour an important factor in their vote in the recent US midterm elections, where Republicans were dealt massive losses with the cost of living a key issue for voters.

“Washington has allowed the federal minimum wage to become increasingly disconnected from the economic reality facing American families,” Saru Jayaraman, president of One Fair Wage, said in a statement.

The push for the Living Wage For All Act comes as Democrats prepare to take control of both the House and Senate in the new Congress.

The last major attempt to raise the federal minimum wage came during former President Joe Biden’s first year in office. Democrats sought to increase the rate from $7.25 to $15 an hour through the Raise the Wage Act of 2021, which was included in the original proposal for Biden’s American Rescue Plan.

Ultimately, the effort failed after the Senate rejected a motion to waive budgetary rules that would have allowed the minimum-wage increase to proceed. The March 2021 vote was 42–58, with all Republicans opposed, joined by seven Democrats and independent Senator Angus King of Maine, who caucuses with Democrats.

Although the legislation failed, Biden raised the minimum wage for federal contract workers to $15 an hour in 2022 through an executive order. President Donald Trump revoked that order in 2025.

برای کارفرمایان بزرگتر - آنهایی که بیش از 500 کارمند در سراسر کشور دارند یا حداقل یک میلیارد دلار درآمد سالانه دارند - این افزایش تا سال 2031 تکمیل خواهد شد. کارفرمایان کوچکتر تا سال 2038 فرصت خواهند داشت. پس از آن، حداقل دستمزد در دو سوم متوسط ​​دستمزد ساعتی ایالات متحده باقی می ماند و با تعدیل سالانه برای حفظ این نسبت.

news.originalContent:
Pete Hegseth says the agreement will include joint training and intelligence sharing with the Venezuelan military.

United States Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth has announced a new agreement with Venezuela’s interim government to facilitate military cooperation between the two countries.

The Pentagon chief made a surprise visit to the Venezuelan capital of Caracas on Wednesday, becoming the latest in a series of high-level officials under US President Donald Trump to travel to the South American country.

During his stop, Hegseth revealed that the deal would include intelligence sharing and joint training for the two countries’ militaries.

“We see this as a reestablishment of our defence partnership and the opportunity to work together between our two great militaries,” he said.

Their shared aim would be “to stabilise Venezuela and rid it of narco-terrorists once and for all”, Hegseth added.

Hegseth was hosted by interim President Delcy Rodriguez, who has led the government since her swearing-in on January 5. His trip was not previously announced by the Pentagon.

The Trump administration has exerted heavy influence over Rodriguez and her government after abducting former President Nicolas Maduro during a military attack on January 3.

Rodriguez was previously Venezuela’s vice president. Trump has justified the attack as a law enforcement effort designed to force Maduro to “stand trial on American soil”, charging him with weapons- and drug-related crimes.

After the operation, Trump also said he planned to “run” Venezuela, and he told The Atlantic magazine that Rodriguez could “pay a very big price, probably bigger than Maduro” if she refuses to comply with US demands.

Since then, he has worked with the Venezuelan government to extract concessions on US priorities such as energy development and military cooperation.

Critics have accused the US of reducing Venezuela to a vassal state and exploiting its resources while leaving Maduro’s government largely intact.

Under Maduro, the Venezuelan state was accused of human rights abuses including torture, arbitrary imprisonment and extrajudicial killings.

Still, Trump has held up Venezuela as a model he would like to see replicated in other countries, like Iran and Cuba.

In Wednesday’s remarks, Hegseth said that the South American country “has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner”.

Rodriguez hailed the agreement as a “resumption of the technical-military relationship between both countries”, and she expressed hope that their cooperation could be “brought to its highest possible level”.

Hegseth is also set to meet with officials in Colombia later on Wednesday as part of a trip to the region.

Colombian Defence Minister Jorge Eduardo Mora said on Tuesday that the US would deliver a C-130 Hercules military aircraft, as the US steps up military involvement across Latin America.

Hegseth has faced pressure to step down from his role, following a midterm election in which the US-Israel war on Iran contributed to Republican losses across the country.

A key member of Trump’s cabinet, Hegseth has championed the war, as well as efforts to weaken rules of engagement designed to limit civilian casualties.

Hegseth narrowly avoided a recent impeachment effort in the US Congress this month. The sponsor of that effort, outgoing Republican US Representative Thomas Massie, cited the Iran war as well as a campaign of military strikes targeting alleged drug trafficking vessels off the coast of Latin America.

The boat-strike campaign has killed an estimated 244 people and has been denounced as extrajudicial killings by legal experts.
news.content: پیت هگزت می گوید که این توافق شامل آموزش مشترک و تبادل اطلاعات با ارتش ونزوئلا می شود. پیت هگزت وزیر دفاع ایالات متحده از توافق جدیدی با دولت موقت ونزوئلا برای تسهیل همکاری نظامی بین دو کشور خبر داده است. رئیس پنتاگون روز چهارشنبه یک سفر غیرمنتظره به کاراکاس پایتخت ونزوئلا داشت و آخرین نفر از یک سری مقامات بلندپایه تحت ریاست دونالد ترامپ رئیس جمهور آمریکا بود که به این کشور آمریکای جنوبی سفر کرد. هگزت در طول این سفر فاش کرد که این توافق شامل تبادل اطلاعات و آموزش مشترک برای نظامیان دو کشور خواهد بود. هگزت افزود: «ما این را به منزله برقراری مجدد مشارکت دفاعی خود و فرصتی برای همکاری بین دو ارتش بزرگ خود می‌دانیم. هدف مشترک آنها «تثبیت ونزوئلا و خلاصی از شر تروریست‌های مواد مخدر یک‌بار برای همیشه» خواهد بود. قبلا توسط پنتاگون اعلام شده بود. دولت ترامپ پس از ربودن نیکلاس مادورو، رئیس‌جمهور سابق در جریان حمله نظامی در 3 ژانویه، نفوذ زیادی بر رودریگز و دولت او اعمال کرده است. رودریگز قبلا معاون رئیس‌جمهور ونزوئلا بود. ترامپ این حمله را به عنوان تلاشی برای اجرای قانون برای وادار کردن مادورو به «محاکمه در خاک آمریکا» و متهم کردن او به جنایات مرتبط با سلاح و مواد مخدر توجیه کرده است.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Omar Havana/Getty Images)

Germany and Britain publicly rebuked a senior Pentagon official Tuesday after he criticized Ukraine’s attacks deep inside Russia.

Ukraine’s long-range strikes have failed to significantly slow Russian advances or bring the conflict closer to an end, Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby said during a Nov. 17 meeting of Ukraine’s military supporters, according to the Department of War. The criticism drew immediate objections from two major NATO allies, whose defense ministers defended Ukraine’s strategy during a subsequent NATO press conference.

Criticizing Ukrainian attacks against strategic military facilities inside Russia was “quite a stupid thing,” German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said during the NATO press conference.

(Photo by Omar Havana/Getty Images)

The dispute unfolded during a meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group at NATO headquarters in Brussels, where Western officials gathered to coordinate additional military assistance ahead of winter, according to NATO. (RELATED: Ukraine’s War Goes Underground As Troops Battle Inside Gas Pipelines)

Ukraine’s campaign against Russian infrastructure has received considerable attention but has not produced meaningful battlefield results, Colby argued, according to his official remarks.

Attacks against civilian commercial facilities could also strengthen Russian public support for the war and increase Moscow’s willingness to escalate, he warned, per the Department of War.

The Pentagon official specifically referenced Ukrainian strikes against warehouses operated by Wildberries, one of Russia’s largest online retailers, according to the Department of War.

Ukraine has accused Wildberries of supplying equipment and technical components used by Russian forces, allegations the company denies, the Associated Press reported.

Western governments should instead concentrate on Russia’s repeated attacks against Ukrainian electricity, water and heating infrastructure, Pistorius argued, according to NATO.

Ukraine’s long-range operations have weakened Russia’s ability to sustain its invasion while giving Ukrainian forces additional time to defend themselves, British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting said during the same NATO press conference.

The operations have helped save Ukrainian lives by degrading Russia’s military capabilities, Streeting maintained, according to NATO.

Ukraine’s attacks were responses to Russian bombardments, and Kyiv intends to retaliate even more forcefully against future strikes, Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara said, according to Reuters.

Ukraine also intends to more than triple its long-range strike capabilities next year, Khmara announced, Reuters reported, citing the Ukrainian Defense Minister.

Despite criticizing certain attacks, the Pentagon did not call for Ukraine to abandon strikes inside Russia altogether.

(Photo by Omar Havana/Getty Images)

Instead, American assistance should prioritize frontline defensive operations and medium-range strikes against Russian logistics networks, Colby argued, according to his official remarks.

The disagreement also highlighted differences over Ukraine’s military strategy as European governments assume greater responsibility for financing American weapons deliveries under President Donald Trump. (RELATED: EU Pushes Massive New Weapons Buying Spree With Ukraine)

European allies and Canada have increasingly financed purchases of American military equipment for Ukraine through NATO’s Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List initiative, according to NATO

Allies have pledged more than $10 billion through that program and other American military sales arrangements for Ukraine, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said during the press conference.

Additional air defense systems, missiles, ammunition and drones remain essential as Russia continues attacking Ukrainian cities and infrastructure, Rutte said, per NATO.

Washington nevertheless remains committed to reaching a negotiated end to the conflict, even as officials prepare for the possibility that Russian military operations will continue through winter, according to the Department of War.

(عکس از عمر هاوانا/گتی ایماژ) به گفته ناتو، این اختلاف در جریان نشست گروه تماس دفاعی اوکراین در مقر ناتو در بروکسل، جایی که مقامات غربی برای هماهنگی کمک‌های نظامی بیشتر قبل از زمستان گرد هم آمدند، آشکار شد. (مرتبط: جنگ اوکراین زیرزمینی می شود زیرا سربازان در داخل خطوط لوله گاز نبرد می کنند) طبق اظهارات رسمی وی، کولبی استدلال کرد که کمپین اوکراین علیه زیرساخت های روسیه توجه قابل توجهی را به خود جلب کرده است، اما نتایج میدان نبرد معناداری را به همراه نداشته است. او هشدار داد که حملات علیه تأسیسات تجاری غیرنظامی همچنین می تواند حمایت عمومی روسیه از جنگ را تقویت کند و تمایل مسکو را برای تشدید تشدید کند.

news.originalContent:
Israeli tanks advance beyond the ‘Yellow Line’, forcing Palestinians to flee again as Gaza faces a deepening humanitarian crisis.

Israeli forces have launched a ground operation in central Gaza, advancing west of the line they withdrew to under last year’s ceasefire and forcing Palestinian families, many of whom had already been displaced, to flee their homes once again.

The operation, the first major ground offensive publicly announced by the Israeli military since the ceasefire took effect on October 10, 2025, follows a warning by the United States-backed Board of Peace that the 13-month-old agreement risks collapse. In a report to the United Nations Security Council, the board accused Israel of restricting aid and delaying the deployment of Palestinian police, and Hamas of continuing armed activity and taxing goods entering Gaza. Senior Hamas official Basem Naim dismissed the report as “pure disinformation”.

Israeli tanks and bulldozers advanced towards Salah al-Din Street, Gaza’s main north-south route, east of the Nuseirat refugee camp and north of the Bureij refugee camp, Al Jazeera correspondents reported. Palestinians fled those areas, amid heavy gunfire and artillery shelling.

The Israeli military body overseeing civilian affairs in the occupied Palestinian territory, known as COGAT, said the army had closed that stretch of Salah al-Din Street and told residents to stay away until further notice. The army hasn’t said how long the operation will last.

An Israeli attack on al-Mughraqa killed one person and wounded several others, an official at al-Awda Hospital told Al Jazeera. Separate attacks in Deir el-Balah, Nuseirat and Gaza City killed three more people.

“We fear this may be the start of a broader operation and that displacement will begin anew, as we have not yet recovered from the effects of the previous war and displacement,” Mahmoud al-Saafin, a 27-year-old resident of Bureij, told the AFP news agency.

The areas targeted in the operation lie west of the “Yellow Line”, where Israeli troops pulled back to under the first phase of President Donald Trump’s plan, leaving them in about 53 percent of Gaza. Israel has, however, continued to move that line gradually, and it now encompasses around two-thirds of the enclave. More than two million Palestinians live in the rest, mostly in tents.

The military told AFP it had launched “a precise operation” west of the line “to remove a threat” posed to the Israeli army, adding that “there is Hamas infrastructure in the area, adding it was responding to Hamas ceasefire violations.

“We reserve the freedom to act and manoeuvre whenever necessary to eliminate any immediate threat in the Gaza Strip,” the army said.

Israel says Hamas has been regrouping and rearming, and it has stepped up attacks. On Saturday, an Israeli attack killed Samir Abu Younis, the Qassam Brigades’ Rafah commander.

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said Israel won’t withdraw until Hamas is dismantled. “If tensions escalate on the various fronts, we are fully prepared to seize additional territory, evacuate local residents and incorporate it into Israel’s permanent security perimeter,” he said.

Hamas called the operation and the forced evacuations northeast of Nuseirat “a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement”, and urged mediators to “intervene immediately”.

It accused Israel of “systematically” squeezing Palestinians into a narrow area of Gaza, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s caretaker government of escalating to escape its domestic crises.

Hamas also condemned the Board of Peace for having “unacceptably equated the occupation’s ongoing aggression with the suffering of the Palestinian victim”.

The Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine called the operation a “prelude” to a wider escalation aimed at forcibly displacing Palestinians.

Israeli forces have kept up near-daily attacks, shelling and home demolitions. Gaza’s Ministry of Health says they have killed 1,658 Palestinians and wounded 6,000 since the ceasefire began. The Israeli military says five of its soldiers have been killed in the same period, the Reuters news agency reports.

On Tuesday alone, Israeli fire killed six Palestinians, including a six-year-old boy, Gaza’s civil defence agency and hospitals told AFP.

Aid remains restricted. About 100,000 tents are waiting to enter Gaza, held up by crossing closures and lengthy Israeli security checks, the International Organization for Migration says.

The ceasefire halted major fighting, but the rest of the plan, covering Israel’s withdrawal, reconstruction and Hamas’s disarmament, has stalled. Hamas agreed in July to a roadmap to give up its weapons and hand over governance. Israel rejected it.

Israel also hasn’t let the board’s technocratic administration start work in Gaza. That has held up an international stabilisation force, The Associated Press news agency reported.

The board spelled out what failure would mean. “Should it collapse, there would be no road map to return to, no administration to deploy and no enabling environment to rebuild.”

news.originalContent:
The report projects steady increases for both Christianity and Islam from 2020 to 2070.

Islam will soon be the world’s largest religion, taking Christianity’s place by 2035, according to the Pew Research Center.

The research organisation assessed the Muslim population’s expected growth in a report released on Tuesday, which projected that both groups will see their numbers increase over the next few decades.

However, the Muslim population will “simply [grow] at a faster pace,” the report said.

The projection analysed 201 countries and territories, accounting for 99.98 percent of the population, and spanned the geographic distribution and future changes of seven religious groups and affiliations – Muslims, Christians, Jews, Hindus, Buddhists, and others – from the years 2020 to 2070.

The results are part of the Pew-Templeton Global Religious Futures Project, which seeks to analyse religious change and its impact on the world.

The organisation stressed that the findings are “not intended to predict all the ways the world could change” as several other events might occur that could impact a group’s religious affiliation, such as socioeconomic circumstances, natural disasters, and wars.

According to the report, Muslims give birth to the highest number of children, one of the factors that Pew says make them the world’s fastest-growing religious group.

Fertility rates were found to be 3.1 children per Muslim woman, while Christians, with the second-highest fertility rate, had 2.5 children per Christian woman.

A generation can typically replace itself with a fertility rate of around 2.1 children per woman.

Both groups are expected to “keep pace with the world’s overall population growth”, according to Pew.

Muslims could gain up to 1.6 billion people through natural population change, compared to 792 million people for Christians.

Muslims are expected to have much smaller losses in their community than Christians leaving or converting religions.

“The difference between the number of people who join and leave Islam is expected to result in a loss of 8 million people during the projection period, [whereas] for Christians, the net difference is a projected loss of 105 million people,” the report said.

Those who choose to depart from Christianity may not identify with a religion afterwards, including atheists and agnostics.

However, the research finds that Islam’s projected growth is not the result of people converting from Christianity: the number of Muslims projected to convert to Christianity is only “slightly greater” than the number of Christians expected to become Muslims.

Between 2020 and 2070, “most of the growth in the world’s Muslim population is projected to occur in places where Muslims already make up a majority of the population”, said Pew.

By 2070, Muslims will make up 95 percent of the population in the Middle East-North Africa region. Meanwhile, in the Asia-Pacific region, Muslims are expected to surpass the religiously unaffiliated.

Muslims were the majority religious group in 53 countries in 2020. An additional 1.2 billion Muslims are expected to live in these countries by 2070, representing 74 percent of the projected growth of the global Muslim population.

For instance, Pakistan’s Muslim population is expected to double from 227 million in 2020 to 461 million in 2070. The country will become the world’s largest Muslim population, overtaking Indonesia, Pew said.

Christian growth will also be concentrated across 120 countries where Christians were already the majority of the population.

Overall, the population of Christians in these countries is forecast to rise by 630 million, representing 92 percent of global Christian growth.
news.content: طبق گزارش مرکز تحقیقاتی پیو، این گزارش افزایش مستمری را برای مسیحیت و اسلام از سال 2020 تا 2070 پیش‌بینی می‌کند. طبق گزارش مرکز تحقیقاتی پیو، اسلام به زودی بزرگترین دین جهان خواهد شد و تا سال 2035 جای مسیحیت را خواهد گرفت. سازمان تحقیقاتی در گزارشی که روز سه‌شنبه منتشر شد، رشد مورد انتظار جمعیت مسلمانان را ارزیابی کرد و پیش‌بینی کرد که تعداد هر دو گروه در چند دهه آینده افزایش خواهد یافت. با این حال، در این گزارش آمده است که جمعیت مسلمانان «به سادگی با سرعت بیشتری [رشد] خواهد شد.» این پیش‌بینی 201 کشور و منطقه را که 99.98 درصد جمعیت را تشکیل می‌دهند، تحلیل کرد و توزیع جغرافیایی و تغییرات آتی هفت گروه و وابستگی مذهبی - مسلمانان، مسیحیان، یهودیان، هندوها، بودایی‌ها و سایرین را از 20-20 تا سال‌ها در بر گرفت. نتایج بخشی از پروژه آینده‌های مذهبی جهانی Pew-Templeton است که به دنبال تجزیه و تحلیل تغییرات مذهبی و تأثیر آن بر جهان است. این سازمان تأکید کرد که یافته‌ها «به منظور پیش‌بینی تمام راه‌هایی که جهان می‌تواند تغییر کند» نیست، زیرا ممکن است چندین رویداد دیگر رخ دهد که می‌تواند بر وابستگی مذهبی یک گروه تأثیر بگذارد، مانند شرایط اجتماعی-اقتصادی، جنگ‌ها و بلایای طبیعی. بر اساس این گزارش، مسلمانان بیشترین تعداد فرزند را به دنیا می آورند، یکی از عواملی که پیو می گوید آنها را به سریع ترین گروه مذهبی در جهان تبدیل می کند. نرخ باروری به ازای هر زن مسلمان 3.1 فرزند است، در حالی که مسیحیان، با دومین نرخ باروری، h.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Alex Wong/Getty Images)

The House of Representatives will skip town early for the Thanksgiving recess while several issues remain unresolved.

The House canceled votes initially scheduled for Friday without addressing several unresolved issues, such as affordability, government funding and the national debt. Republicans have limited time to finish their agenda before Democrats take over.

Congress has yet to reach an agreement on government funding past the Dec. 11 deadline. Some Democrats suggested they would not agree to passing a continuing resolution (CR) if the Iran war continued. (RELATED: House Skipping Town Early As SAVE America Act Saga Continues To Rock Capitol Hill)

News: House GOP leadership cancels votes on Friday

The House has not addressed artificial intelligence (AI) safety after a series of recent cyberattacks and tech outages. Tech engineers and prominent AI researchers resigned from major labs in September and warned that AI development must be slowed to prevent the technology from killing humanity.

Neither chamber passed bills addressing automated license plate readers (ALPRs), including Flock Safety cameras. Several lawmakers introduced bills to restrict Flock cameras, though none would enforce an outright ban.

A third reconciliation bill, the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) and the farm bill have yet to reach President Donald Trump’s desk as they await passage in the Senate.

The national debt surpassed $40 trillion in August, yet lawmakers have not taken action to address it. The third reconciliation bill costs $95 billion and includes no offsets. It passed the House in July and has yet to be taken up by the Senate.

The package includes $10 billion for the House Administration Committee to hand out grants to implement the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) America Act, $73 billion for the House Armed Services Committee and House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence to address the Iran war and $12 billion to aid struggling farmers. It includes no spending offsets and would not address the $1.4 trillion deficit.

The Senate is likely to take up a major permitting reform bill aiming to lower energy costs by speeding up federal reviews of energy and infrastructure. If it passes the Senate, the House would need to approve the upper chamber’s changes before it reaches Trump’s desk.

The affordability crisis remains unresolved after the midterm elections. Democrats secured major victories in both chambers as voters disapproved of Trump’s handling of affordability.

(عکس از الکس وانگ/گتی ایماژ)
مجلس نمایندگان زودتر از زمان تعطیلات روز شکرگزاری از شهر خارج خواهد شد در حالی که چندین موضوع حل نشده باقی مانده است. مجلس رای گیری هایی را که در ابتدا برای جمعه برنامه ریزی شده بود، بدون پرداختن به چندین موضوع حل نشده، مانند استطاعت، بودجه دولتی و بدهی ملی لغو کرد. جمهوری خواهان زمان محدودی برای تکمیل دستور کار خود قبل از روی کار آمدن دموکرات ها دارند. کنگره هنوز در مورد بودجه دولتی پس از ضرب الاجل 11 دسامبر به توافق نرسیده است. برخی از دموکرات‌ها پیشنهاد کردند که در صورت ادامه جنگ با ایران، با ادامه قطعنامه (CR) موافقت نخواهند کرد. (مرتبط: خانه پرش از شهر در اوایل با ادامه حماسه قانون نجات آمریکا به کاپیتول هیل)
خبر: رهبری مجلس نمایندگان مجلس آرای روز جمعه را لغو کرد پس از یک سری حملات سایبری اخیر و قطعی فناوری، مجلس به ایمنی هوش مصنوعی (AI) توجهی نکرده است. مهندسان فناوری و محققان برجسته هوش مصنوعی در ماه سپتامبر از آزمایشگاه‌های اصلی استعفا دادند و هشدار دادند که توسعه هوش مصنوعی باید کند شود تا از کشتن بشریت جلوگیری شود. چندین قانونگذار لایحه‌هایی را برای محدود کردن دوربین‌های Flock ارائه کردند، اگرچه هیچ یک ممنوعیت کامل را اجرا نمی‌کنند. سومین لایحه مصالحه، قانون مجوز دفاع ملی (NDAA) و لایحه مزرعه هنوز به میز رئیس‌جمهور دونالد ترامپ نرسیده‌اند، زیرا در انتظار تصویب در سنا هستند. بدهی ملی در ماه اوت از 40 تریلیون دلار فراتر رفت.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Matt RAMEY / AFP via Getty Images)

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s business ties are drawing scrutiny amid questions over his family’s commercial interests and his role in shaping U.S. tech policy.

The scrutiny around Lutnick has also become intertwined with a broader controversy involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his alleged affair with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese intelligence asset who previously led Megaspeed, a data center operator under investigation for allegedly smuggling advanced chips into China. (RELATED: Jensen Huang Says He’d Be ‘Honored’ To Come Back To Nvidia, One Day After Company Put Kibosh On Reunion)

Beyond the controversy surrounding Nvidia, Lutnick’s own ties to the technology sector have raised questions about the potential overlap between his family’s business interests and U.S. policy toward China.

In Malaysia’s southern peninsula, a data center known as A201 is expected to open next year and house hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia’s most advanced artificial intelligence servers, according to a New York Times (NYT) report.

The facility is expected to provide computing power to a Chinese technology giant, potentially allowing the company to access advanced AI chips through a Southeast Asian data center despite U.S. restrictions on direct sales to Chinese companies.

The company operating A201, Bitdeer, is a client of Cantor Fitzgerald, the financial services firm Lutnick led for nearly 30 years before joining the Trump administration, according to the NYT.

After Lutnick was confirmed as commerce secretary in February 2025 and stepped away from the firm, his sons Brandon and Kyle took over leadership positions, with Brandon becoming chairman and Kyle executive vice chairman of Cantor Fitzgerald, L.P.

Cantor has also maintained business ties with Singapore-based Bitdeer, serving as a sales agent for the company’s equity offering, which was valued at up to $1 billion this year and will operate A201, according to a Bitdeer press release.

The firms’ relationship dates back to at least 2024, when Cantor helped Bitdeer arrange a stock offering of up to $250 million, according to the NYT.

Meanwhile, Howard Lutnick is helping shape the export policies that could determine whether facilities like A201 can continue accessing advanced American AI chips and supplying computing power to Chinese companies. The overlap between his family’s business interests and his role in setting U.S. export policy has raised questions about potential conflicts of interest.

Lutnick has also emerged as a key figure in efforts to slow stricter restrictions on Nvidia chip sales to data centers outside China that serve Chinese clients, putting him at odds with other administration officials, particularly Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

The policy dispute has increasingly spilled into public view, exposing broader divisions within the Trump administration over how aggressively to restrict China’s access to advanced American technology.

Bessent publicly placed responsibility on Lutnick and the Commerce Department Friday for failing to blacklist Megaspeed, the company at the center of the controversy involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a woman suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence. (RELATED: Bessent Throws Lutnick Under The Bus On Trump’s Chip Export Fiasco)

Appearing Friday on CNBC’s Squawk Box, Bessent said the U.S. Trade Representative and the departments of the Treasury, War, State, and the National Security Council (NSC) all supported adding Megaspeed to the Entity List, a federal trade blacklist targeting foreign entities deemed national security or foreign policy risks, leaving the Commerce Department as the point of disagreement.

Howard Lutnick never did it Megaspeed is the Singapore firm run by Alice Huang, the suspected CHINESE SPY tied to ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang "You will have to ask [Commerce] about their internal process…I am frustrated when President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s. And so any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies and the AI race, gives the Chinese an advantage." It spent more than $4 BILLION on Nvidia AI chips and is suspected of smuggling them into China

The key Trump Cabinet officials pushed to tighten restrictions to close a loophole that allowed Chinese companies to access advanced American AI chips by renting computing power from data centers in third countries.

The debate has also intensified scrutiny of Lutnick’s family’s financial ties to the data center industry and his department’s relationship with Nvidia. The company has faced allegations of receiving unusual access to the Commerce Department as it worked to influence U.S. export policy, according to an Axios report.

Lutnick’s relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has especially drawn attention. Recounting a phone call on Joe Rogan’s podcast last December, Huang recalled that Lutnick had called him and described his company as “a national treasure.”

Those questions have taken on added significance following revelations surrounding Huang’s alleged affair with Alice Huang, a Singaporean data center operator under investigation for potential export control violations, according to the Department of Justice (DOJ).

The overlapping business and personal connections have fueled further questions about the relationships between technology executives and administration officials, as well as Lutnick’s influence over the administration’s China policy and decisions governing access to advanced American AI technology.

Against that backdrop, the Commerce Department announced Monday in a post on X that it had issued an interim final rule, “at the direction of the Treasury Department and the National Security Council,” to restrict remote access to advanced American semiconductors and computing systems.

The rule is intended to prevent foreign entities from circumventing existing U.S. export restrictions by accessing sensitive American technology through cloud computing services and data centers located in third countries.

The announcement coincided with a separate disclosure that the Commerce Department had been investigating Megaspeed for potential export control violations since 2024.

In a late Monday post on X, the department said investigators requested records from Nvidia in May 2025 concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed.

The following month, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list. Bureau of Industry and Security agents later conducted an in-person end-use check at the company alongside Singaporean law enforcement officials and interviewed its CEO, Alice Huang.

Lutnick praised the agency’s work in response to the department’s post on X, writing, “The Department of Commerce works to protect the U.S. economy and our critical industries every day. We are very proud of the work of the Bureau of Industry and Security.”

The Commerce Department has said Lutnick complied with ethics agreements. There is no evidence that Cantor Fitzgerald’s business dealings influenced Lutnick’s policy decisions, despite the scrutiny surrounding the firm’s financial relationships, according to CNN and the NYT reports.

The Department of Commerce works to protect the U.S. economy and our critical industries every day. We are very proud of the work of the Bureau of Industry and Security.

Both Bessent and Lutnick are traveling with President Donald Trump on his trip to China, where the president is scheduled to meet with the President of the People’s Republic of China, Xi Jinping, this week.

The dispute reflects a broader divide within the Trump administration over how aggressively to restrict advanced AI chip sales to Southeast Asian data centers that could provide Chinese companies with a workaround to U.S. export controls.

While China hawks like Bessent have pushed for tighter restrictions, Lutnick has favored a less restrictive approach, seeking to preserve business opportunities for American companies such as Nvidia.

Trump acknowledged the differences between the two officials when asked by CNN White House Correspondent Alayna Treene on Monday, ahead of his trip to China, saying they have “a different viewpoint” on the country. (RELATED: Nvidia’s Latest Move Signals Board Knows More To Story Than They’re Letting On)

“One wants to be friendly with China, and one wants to have a blowup with China,” Trump told Treene Monday.

House Democrats are also launching a probe seeking records of Cantor Fitzgerald’s Nvidia trades since Jan. 1, 2024, and information about any personal Nvidia investments held by Lutnick and Trump, according to a Politico report.

The inquiry comes as Cantor’s Nvidia holdings have declined since early 2025. Cantor spokesperson Danielle Popper told Politico the firm “holds no material proprietary position in Nvidia,” attributing the decline to the unwinding of client equity swaps rather than a decision to sell off a proprietary investment. She also called allegations that Cantor influenced government policy “baseless.”

Cantor Fitzgerald & Co., the firm’s investment-banking arm, also drew scrutiny in July 2025, several months after President Trump’s April 2025 Liberation Day tariff announcement, after reportedly offering companies that paid tariffs the opportunity to sell their rights to potential refunds for 20 to 30 cents on the dollar, according to a WIRED report.

Documents reviewed by the outlet allegedly show that Cantor could have facilitated hundreds of millions of dollars in such transactions, with at least one deal worth about $10 million already completed.

The arrangement could have let investors bet that courts would eventually strike down the tariffs, potentially generating returns of three to five times their initial investment.

The Supreme Court ultimately ruled 6-3 on Feb. 20, 2026, that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) does not authorize the president to impose tariffs.

Cantor Fitzgerald has denied completing any tariff-refund transactions or taking positions on the tariffs’ legality. In an emailed statement to WIRED, Erica Chase, a spokesperson for the firm, said, “Cantor is not in the business of positioning any risk or taking views in litigation claims, including tariffs.” Semafor later reported that Cantor Fitzgerland considered the tariff investment arrangement but declined to proceed.

The Daily Caller also asked the Commerce Department about allegations that Lutnick’s sons positioned business deals ahead of Trump’s April 2 Liberation Day tariff announcement and may have received advance notice of impending administration actions.

In response, a department spokesperson said, “The Secretary has fully complied with the terms of his ethics agreement, including all divestiture and recusal requirements, and will continue to do so. He has divested all financial interests in Cantor Fitzgerald, Newmark, and BGC.”

Cantor Fitzgerald took out a net $2.7 billion short position on U.S. Treasuries the same month as Trump’s Liberation Day tariff announcement, April 2025.

The Caller also reached out to Cantor Fitzgerald for comment on the allegations involving Howard Lutnick’s sons.

A Cantor spokesperson provided the following statement, writing, “Cantor never executed trades related to the tariffs, has never received revenue of any kind in this market, and has never taken any position concerning enforceability of the tariffs or the value of tariff refund claims. Cantor never received any material nonpublic information concerning the enforceability of the tariffs from Secretary Lutnick or anyone else.”

Former Vice President Mike Pence is offering conservatives an impossible path forward after the Republican Party’s historic bloodbath in the 2026 midterms: turning back time.

During a speech delivered at the libertarian Cato Institute on Tuesday, Pence called on conservatives to embrace limited government, fiscal discipline, “free markets,” and a hawkish foreign policy, rather than economic “populism,” protectionist tariffs, and non-interventionist restraint. In other words, he wants the Republican Party to return to the pre-Trump status quo.
